description: A model of the four-pole transistor ladder filter built around the 4072 board, taken from the circuit itself, with a drive control into the ladder and two attenuverted cutoff CV inputs

params.text: Sets the cutoff, which the maker's tooltip gives as 20Hz to 14.5kHz; the resonant peak stays noticeably below the marked corner until the resonance is well up, which is a trait of the circuit
Sets the level of the signal going into the ladder, from silence to unity; the ladder saturates on its own, so this is the module's main tone control
Sets the resonance; the filter self-oscillates in the last 8% of the travel, the figure the maker's own tooltip prints
Attenuates and inverts the CV-1 input before it reaches the cutoff
Attenuates and inverts the CV-2 input before it reaches the cutoff

inputs.text: Moves the cutoff, scaled by the CV-1 knob above it
Moves the cutoff a volt per octave, so a self-oscillating filter can be played from a keyboard
Moves the cutoff, scaled by the CV-2 knob above it
The audio put through the ladder

notes: every jack takes polyphony, and the number of channels is the wider of the V/OCT and INPUT channel counts, up to sixteen; a monophonic cable in any jack is read by every channel
the current mirror in the model weights the two collector currents unequally, which is where the even harmonics this circuit is known for come from
